title: Fan interview: running a 2,000-member anime club
summary: A short Q&A with Tolu, organiser of Lagos Anime Watch Night.
guest: Tolu, organiser of Lagos Anime Watch Night

transcript.q: How did the watch nights start?
transcript.a: Four of us watching Demon Slayer on a laptop in a hostel room. People kept knocking on the door, so we moved outside.

transcript.q: What is the hardest part of organising?
transcript.a: Picking the episodes. Everybody has a favourite arc and nobody agrees.

transcript.q: Advice for someone starting a club?
transcript.a: Start small, keep it free and let people bring their own snacks. The community builds itself.

title: Fan interview: speedrunning on a budget
summary: A short Q&A with Daniel, speedrunner and stream host.

transcript.a: Watching a marathon at 2am and thinking, I know a faster route than that.
No. My first personal best was on a second-hand console and a phone camera.
Anything with movement tech. Learning a new skip feels better than beating a boss.

title: Fan interview: leading a dance cover crew
summary: A short Q&A with Amara, captain of a K-Pop dance cover team.
guest: Amara, captain of a K-Pop dance cover team

transcript.q: How long does one cover take?
transcript.a: About three weeks for a four-minute song if everyone practises.
Formations. Everyone learns the moves, but moving between spots is where it falls apart.
Learn from the mirrored practice video and film yourself early.

title: Fan interview: drawing your first comic page
summary: A short Q&A with Kemi, illustrator at the Draw Your Hero workshop.
guest: Kemi, illustrator at the Draw Your Hero workshop

transcript.a: Thumbnails. Tiny, messy sketches of the whole page before any detail.
Paper first. It teaches you to commit to a line.
Miles Morales. It showed me a hero can look like the kids on my street.
